rows.question: Why is Qassim warehouse 35% more expensive to run than comparable sites?

payload.question: Why is Qassim warehouse 35% more expensive to run than comparable sites?
payload.answer: Qassim’s higher reported cost appears to be driven mainly by cost allocation and utilities, with a possible labor-efficiency component. Pharmacy Retail’s co-location utilities remained in Tamween’s cost base until a SAR 4.43M intercompany recharge was settled. Tamween also recorded utilities pressure from the broader tariff step and payroll pressure from warehouse overtime and Saudisation. The evidence does not include a site-by-site peer cost bridge, so it cannot quantify how much of the reported gap remains after correcting the recharge or attribute the gap among energy, labor, throughput and facility utilization.
payload.basis: The remediation record directly identifies unrecharged Qassim co-location utilities. The H1 cost-variance records identify tariff and co-location effects in utilities and warehouse overtime plus Saudisation in payroll. Independent confirmation requires comparable-site operating costs and normalized activity measures such as throughput, storage requirements, occupied space and labor hours.
payload.why: The remediation record directly identifies unrecharged Qassim co-location utilities. The H1 cost-variance records identify tariff and co-location effects in utilities and warehouse overtime plus Saudisation in payroll. Independent confirmation requires comparable-site operating costs and normalized activity measures such as throughput, storage requirements, occupied space and labor hours.

citations.excerpt: Historic: Qassim co-location utilities unrecharged; backdated intercompany recharge to Mizan Pharmacy Retail; SAR 4,429,534 settled intercompany.
Utilities & Energy: Tariff step BU-wide + Qassim unrecharged co-location (division 1.7 of this).
Payroll: Saudisation Apr step + warehouse overtime (division 1.1, other regions 1.0).

suggestions: Restate Qassim’s site costs after the intercompany recharge and compare them with peer warehouses using consistent throughput, storage, occupancy and labor measures.
Review overtime by shift and activity level to determine whether a residual operating-efficiency issue remains.
Implement a monthly co-location recharge control to keep Retail utilities out of Tamween’s warehouse cost base.

rows.question: How does each BU's margin compare to its listed peers?

payload.question: How does each BU's margin compare to its listed peers?
payload.answer: On the 2025 EBITDA-margin peer tables: • Mizan Pharma Manufacturing: 27.4%. Below SPIMACO (30.5%), Jamjoom (29.5%), Tabuk (28.0%), Hikma (31.0%), Sanofi (35.0%) and Pfizer Saudi (36.0%); above Julphar (24.0%). • Tamween Pharma Distribution: 6.8%. Equal to Banaja (6.8%); above Tamer (6.5%), Boots Saudi Arabia (5.5%) and NUPCO (4.0%); below Al-Olayan Sapaco (7.2%). • Mizan Pharma Logistics: 17.4%. Above Aramex (12.6%), Mohebi (14.0%), DHL Supply Chain Pharma (13.0%), Movianto (15.5%) and GAC Logistics KSA (12.0%); below SAL Saudi Logistics (29.8%). • Mizan Pharmacy Retail: 11.6%. Above United Pharmacies (10.6%), Aman (11.0%) and Innova (10.4%); below Al-Nahdi (13.8%), Whites (12.4%) and Dr Habib Pharmacies (15.5%). • Mizan E-Pharmacy: 6.8%. Below every listed comparator: Al-Nahdi Online (11.4%), Whites Pharmacy Online (9.5%), Aman Pharmacies Online (7.8%) and Care'n Cure UAE (8.5%). • Mizan Digital Health: 19.2%. Above Aster Telehealth (17.2%), Altibbi (15.5%), Cura (18.0%) and Sehhaty (0%); below Whites Connect (22.0%). • Mizan Healthcare Services: 14.6%. Below every listed comparator: Dr Sulaiman Al-Habib (31.0%), Mouwasat (29.5%), Saudi German Hospital (17.0%), Almoosa Specialist (21.0%) and Aster DM Healthcare KSA (15.5%). • Mizan Capital: 40.8%. Above GIB Capital (40.0%) and EFG-Hermes KSA (36.0%); below Jadwa (42.0%), Al Rajhi Capital (48.0%) and SNB Capital (52.0%). The strongest relative position is Pharma Logistics, which exceeds five of six comparators. The clearest gaps are E-Pharmacy and Healthcare Services, both below every supplied comparator. “Listed peers” here means the comparators listed in the workbook; several are private or subsidiaries rather than publicly traded companies.
payload.basis: The comparison uses the supplied 2025 EBITDA percentages from the competitor-financials workbook. No margin gaps or peer medians were newly calculated. The peer table contains some differences from the group BU P&L, so this answer consistently uses the competitor workbook for both Mizan and peers.
payload.why: The comparison uses the supplied 2025 EBITDA percentages from the competitor-financials workbook. No margin gaps or peer medians were newly calculated. The peer table contains some differences from the group BU P&L, so this answer consistently uses the competitor workbook for both Mizan and peers.
suggestions: Prioritize peer-gap plans for E-Pharmacy and Healthcare Services.
Validate comparator relevance for Pharma Logistics because SAL's cargo ground-handling model differs from pharma-focused 3PL operations.
Reconcile the few Mizan margin differences between the competitor workbook and the group BU P&L before board use.
